So real quick over what we're gonna talk about, background on why we're doing this, look at the current process and what we're proposing, the advantages and disadvantages of it and next steps to move this forward. So in 2019, the city hired management partners to review the development process and determine how we could find efficiencies and make the development process go smoother. There were 15 key recommendations that were identified. And one of them identified, I think primarily by the blue team member shown here was a recommendation 13 to, for the city to obtain authority from the DEQ for plan review primacy. So that's what we're proposing to do here with these actions. The current process that we have now for us to approve plans is engineer submits plans, we review them, return them with comments, engineer returns them to us, then we go through and approve them, sign the required forms, return them to the engineer, and then the engineer submits them to the DEQ for approval. That's a 30 to 60 day process currently. So bolding that, so we can come back to that on the next slide. DEQ reviews it with no issues, they issue the permit, then the contractor for the developer can begin work at their desire. So with what we're proposing to do with the ordinance resolutions and then the receipt of the permits is change those things from the previous slide with what was shown here in red. So now we will get the fee from the engineer. We will submit that with the approved plans and forms and we'll eliminate that 30 to 60 day window where DEQ has to review it because they won't have to issue a permit because we'll have that primacy. So advantage of this, obviously the 30 to 60 day review period, we will cut that out. On average, we see about 50 sets of plans, water and sewer a year. So just taking the low end of that, we'll save 1500 days of review time from DEQ annually. So that will let those developers move forward quick and more quickly if they would prefer to do that.
